title: Difference of root-string endpoints is the Cartan integer
statement: Let $I$ be finite, let $V,W$ be vector spaces over $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-field], and let $P:\mathrm{RootPairing}\ I\ \mathbf Q\ V\ W$ be a crystallographic root pairing in the Mathlib sense: injective root and coroot families with a perfect bilinear pairing, root-coroot value $2$, simultaneous reflection permutations, and integral root-coroot pairings. Let $i,j\in I$ with $P.\mathrm{root}(i),P.\mathrm{root}(j)$ linearly independent over $\mathbf Q$. Put $p=P.\mathrm{chainBotCoeff}(i,j)$ and $q=P.\mathrm{chainTopCoeff}(i,j)$, the largest nonnegative integers with $P.\mathrm{root}(j)-pP.\mathrm{root}(i)$ and $P.\mathrm{root}(j)+qP.\mathrm{root}(i)$ roots. As an equality in $\mathbf Z$, $$p-q=P.\mathrm{pairingIn}\ \mathbf Z\ j\ i.$$ Here the integer on the right is the evaluation of the second root on the first coroot.
